Violation ID: 8286147
Permit API: 003-22172
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Ohio Township
Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 8/24/2026
Comments: The Department conducted a compliance schedule evaluation of this well on 08/24/2026. Per an Order (No. 55 M.D. 2024) issued on March 27, 2025, the Operator of this well was required to plug the well by 3/30/2026. In addition to the plugging requirement, the Operator was required to... 1. Provide the Department with a schedule to complete plugging of the well within 30 days of the date of the Order. 2. Submit a fully completed Form 8000-FM-OG0005, "Notice of Intention by Well Operator to Plug a Well," and a well location plat for the wells to the Department not less than 3 and not more than 15 days before the plugging of each well. The Operator has not provided any correspondence to the Department indicating their intent to plug this well. Specifically, the Operator has failed to provide a schedule to complete the plugging of this well within 30 days of the date of the Order as required, and the well remains abandoned and is not plugged. The violation of OGA3259(1) has been updated to OGA3259(2I) and remains outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8226506
Permit API: 015-23923
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On 03/21/2025 the DEP received a spill/release on the pad surface notification (CTS #387689) from representative Steve Moyer. Steve stated "they noticed a stain about 45' x 25' next to the wellheads off containment on gravel. The conductivity was high. Estimating about 1 to 1.5 barrels of produced water was released. An environmental consultant was contacted who will scrape up material." On 03/24/2025 at 0750 hours the DEP spoke with representative Steve Moyer. He stated that there was a leak within the secondary containment that led to this release. A crew scraped the material on 03/21/2025. New gravel has be placed in the 45' x 25' reported release area (photo #2). Upon further investigation it was determined that a crew had been onsite pumping brine down a well to stop the flow to be able to change the wellhead master valve. After they completed work and the area began to dry out a crystal staining was observed. On 03/24/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection for Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) STETHERS Location Well Pad in Wyalusing Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and cloudy. I arrived at 0940 hours. A representative onsite stated the recovered material from the 03/21/2025 release was removed from the site the same day. Recovered material from the 01/29/2025 discovered release (Inspection Report #3907635 and 3919693) was also being removed from the site on 03/21/2025 and continued to be removed during the incident response inspection report on 03/24/2025 (photo #10).Due to the quantity of the release this is being referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance. Violations against API #015-23923 (Inspection Report #3907635 and 3919693, Enforcement ID 437898) remain open:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)Based on the reported release (CTS #387689) additional violations have been cited against API #015-23923: CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1115 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/31/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/31/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 997047
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/31/2023
Comments: Site inspection conducted at the COP Tract 551B pad to review use of EWS VOX4 evaporators for processing flowback water. Meeting on site today with EWS representative Pat Pascarella. There are no EQT personnel on site at time of inspection. A TetraTek crew is loading produced fluid into water trucks. Weather conditions are partly sunny and 73 degrees F. Wind is blowing from the southwest at an estimated 5 mph. Eight EWS Vox4 evaporators are in use at time of inspection. Evaporators process fluid in batches, with automated systems in use to pump water into the system from the production fluid tanks and out to the frac tank batteries when fluid is concentrated. All pipelines and fluid control systems appear to be functioning as designed and there is no fluid or precipitation within evaporator containment. As authorized under the Air Quality Request for Determination Operating Permit, EQT will take four evaporators out of service after the initial 60 days of use. According to Mr. Pascarella, four units will be disconnected on June 13. There are no violations associated with the evaporator authorization. Fluid with elevated conductivity (3.14 mS/cm) is still present at the NE pad sump (photo 7). Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RICE DRILLING B LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/08/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 938981
Permit API: 125-27054
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: North Bethlehem Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/08/2021
Comments: On 12/8/21 an incident inspection of the Brova Well Site was conducted in response to an operator reported spill (CTS ID: 360854). The following was found: >>On 12/4/21 the operator reported that dump line on the site had washed out and failed resulting in a release of more than 5 gallons of produced fluids. >>Inspection of the site on 12/8/21 found a crew on site removing fluid from a trench by the site GPUs. The trench and release were located behind and between a GPU and a large gray cylinder. The trench remained open and partially filled with black watery fluid. Operator estimates of total lost fluids remained unavailable but evidence suggests a spill volume substantially greater than five gallons. The operator reports planning to follow ACT 2 protocols and plans to remove the associated GPU to allow remediation access. This constitutes a violation of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and SWMA 301 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. (Image 1-3) >>One tarped waste box was present on site. (Image 4) >>Wells and other site equipment appeared to be in generally good condition. (Image 5) >>See attached images for an operator description of the incident. (Image 6)

Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 880675
Permit API: 131-20036
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Windham Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-03-13
Comments: At time of inspection, 40 degs. and cloudy. There are (5) wells on this pad. They are the Jack 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H and the 5H, all were in production. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/2" pipe and T'd into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tanks with the exception of the 2H, which is a (2) string well and only has the (9x5) annulus venting to tanks, the (20x9) annulus has an open annulus. All annulus vents are open and venting to production tanks. The cellars had water in them w/ no bubbling observed during insp.. - The Operators well tender (Giovanni Dicupillo) was on site today to isolate the (13x9) annuli of the 1H, 3H and the 4H due to gas being detected in previous inspections. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 3/4/20) was turned on to screen for gas at the isolated annuli and left on to check for gas at cellars, at the well heads and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. No gas was detected at any of the isolated (13x9) annuli or in the ambient air. - The Jack 1H was shut in at time of inspection due to maintenance being performed on GPU by Operator. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off SCADA gauges: - 1H - prod. tree top press.: 1,121 psi., prod. csg. press.: 550.0 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 2.3 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 2.3 psi., and prod. line press.: 2.7 psi. Comments: On September 23, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Apollo Resource's Whyel 1 Well located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following violations issued under inspection report 3875658. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding pending the receipt of the aforementioned documents.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 8241980
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #3978563 conducted on May 15 2025 at 0848. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, or failure. While onsite the well appeared to be producing off of the 4" production string. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 94% combustible gas. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on July 24, 2025. The results were as follows: South and East slam bar holes: Non-detect for combustible gas. North slam bar hole: Peak reading of 3% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. West slam bar hole: Peaking reading of 18% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. Due to the lack of adequate sustained concentration, a viable sample for isotopic analysis could not be collected. On May 22, 2025 the Department received an email from the operator stating that "Titus would prefer to have the Johnson #1 well plugged". As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with it. The Department requests a detailed timeline specifying when the well will be properly plugged or when corrective measures will be undertaken to bring the well into full regulatory compliance.

Comments: An onsite inspection of the Kennedy 4 well was conducted by OGI Pat Hiles. Present during the inspection was Diversified representative Gary Molek and Moody and Associates, Inc. representative Jon Hafer. The Department screened around the 7" casing upon arrival with a Bascom Turner 611. Gas readings of 19%, 6%, and 32% gas was detected at various points surrounding the casing. After further investigation, it appeared that Diversified had poured cement around the exposed 7" casing. Placing cement around the casing does not meet repair standards of 78.86. Once Mr. Molek and Mr. Hafer arrived on location, a commingle pressure of the production casing, tubing, and annulus was garnered using a digital pressure gauge. The commingle pressure recorded was 0.6 psi and this location was used as a sample point by Moody. The wellhead was then reconfigured to conduct an annulus shut in test. At 11:51 the annulus pressure was 0.5 psi before blowing the well down. At 11:55 the annulus pressure was 0.9 psi and the casing blown down. At 12:40 the annulus was at 2.0 psi and blown down to collect a sample. Although pressure was relatively low, there was decent volume. The area surrounding the wellhead was screened for soil gas at intervals of 2 ft, 10 ft, and 20 ft. Soil gas readings from Moody and the Department will be listed below. Landowner has a water well approximately 200 ft from the wellhead. The landowner stated his water well is drilled to a depth of 200 ft. Landowner's water was field screened by Moody and the results were 2% LEL, 2880 ppm, and 5220 ppm. The landowner's basement headspace and water well connections were also screened by Moody with no gas readings detected. Report Details

Permit API: 081-21338
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: On December 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at Seneca Resources Gamble Pad K. No E&S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site is stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are a total of 10 wells capable of producing located on this well pad. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. There are 8 GPUs, 2 line heaters, and 3 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both GPUs, line heaters, and production fluid tanks were stationed in secondary containment. The DEP observed a Seneca Resources contractor pumping water from a well cellar and actively discharging the water off the the pad edge. The contractor provided the log sheet from today's field tests of pH and conductivity of the well cellar. The contractor stated that one well cellar is recorded on the log sheet due to the contractor logging only the highest conductivity of the 10 well cellars tested. The contractor stated that they had pumped out 7 of the well cellars prior to DEP arrival. The well cellar water was being discharged off the North pad edge. Well cellar water that was discharged had only travelled about 15 ft. downslope off the pad edge. There was no estimate of the amount of water pumped out of the 7 other well cellars prior to the DEP arrival.The discharge of water from a well cellar off the well pad is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 91.34(a).

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both well pads. I inspected Pad A first. The 6 wells on Pad A are still in flowback. In the sump on the pad which had been installed after fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC), strontium, and aluminum was discovered, the EC was approximately 800 uS/cm. The Department recommends scraping these stains from the pad surface and disposing of the material appropriately. I showed Mr. Mann the location of these stains during this inspection and he said that he would have both stains scraped immediately. Violations remain outstanding for the diesel mud release on Pad B described in the 8/9/21 inspection number 3231577 by DEP WQS Brad Kline.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-12
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. All contaminated soil was removed from the site and the clean up area was top soiled and stabilized with seed and mulch. All disturbed area restored with a good growth of vegetation growing in October until cold weather. A ditch was cut west through the field from the culvert discharge with no E&S controls which has resulted in erosion of the ditch. E&S controls have been installed on this site in the areas of concentrated flow. There are still several areas in the restored area that show evidence of concentrated flow and erosion. These areas, as well as the entire restored site need to be inspected and maintained until there is enough vegetation growth to stabilize the area. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

Comments: On April 17, 2026, an on-site meeting was held at the operator's request at the Sproul well pad in Stewart Township, Fayette County. The purpose of this meeting was to assess current vegetative growth and review areas lacking 70% vegetative growth coverage. This also a follow-up inspection to IR 4176234.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was executed between the DEP and the operator on 12/16/2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. The 12/16/2021 COA states that the operator "shall restore the Sproul 7005 Site in accordance with the restoration plan in the expired Sproul ESCGP, including but not limited to the installation of all Post Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices ("PCSM BMPs"). Restoration of the Sproul 7005 Well Site shall be completed by 10/30/2025." The operator shall then "submit a Notice of Termination ("NOT") for the Sproul ESCGP once permanent vegetation has been established at the Well Site in accordance with 25 Pa. Code 102.7. The NOT shall be submitted to the DEP no later than 12/31/2025.A Notice of Termination (NOT) request was submitted to the DEP by the operator on December 31, 2025.A notarized Post-Drilling Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration and the updated map requested in IR 4085078 were submitted with the operator's NOT request on December 31, 2025. However, the DEP observed possible soil cracking and soil displacement on the slope north of the well pad on January 5, 2026, at the time of IR 4119144. The operator reported on January 16, 2026, that they conducted repairs in this location and provided a photo of the repairs (IR 4128095). It appeared in the photo provided by the operator that the repair resulted in ground disturbances, as they applied temporary stabilization after completing their repairs. Therefore, the NOT request was denied on January 30, 2026 (IR 4133379).A violation was issued on February 10, 2026, for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 COA (IR 4140173).The following was observed during the inspection:Daugherty reported that they seeded the areas on site that exhibit less than 70% vegetative growth coverage prior to the DEP's arrival to site (photo 8). Daugherty also identified the reported areas on site that have been disturbed by third-party dirt bikes. These locations appears to exhibit approximately 50% vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection (photos 5 and 7). The location where the potential soil cracking and developing soil displacement was observed at the time of IR 4140173 has established additional vegetative growth (photo 6). It appears to exhibit approximately 50% vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. This location does not appear to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth and/or well head integrity at the time of inspection. The potential soil cracking and developing soil displacement were not identifiable during this inspection, and no evidence of further potential soil displacement was observed. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 3 and 4). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a55. Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4140173 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: Chief Oil & Gas reported a release of approximately 2 barrels of produced fluid at the Czop Pad on 2/21/20. The release occurred the same day it was reported. I arrived onsite at 10:05 on 2/24/20. I talked with Kellon Balum and Darrin, both of Chief when I arrived. The release occurred when a piece of the B section of the well broke and allowed produced fluid to begin to spray onto the pad (Photo #1, center). This section of the wellhead is not typically used and doesn't receive much gas flow. It usually is used for monitoring certain pressures in the well. It is believed that sand flowing up from the well eroded and weakened a portion of the pipe and allowed it to rupture. Gas, at approximately 700 to 800 psi pushed produced fluid through the opening, about 2 inches in diameter. This mist was somewhat directional but was blown over a large portion of the pad by wind. The release occurred sometime between a crew leaving the site and the site operator, Darrin, arriving. This limits the duration of the release to no more than about 1 hour. Based on the time and rate of release Chief believes approximately 2 barrels of fluid were released. Typically, offsite monitoring equipment is used to detect events such as this, however, equipment was frozen, and the event was undetected. Much of the pad was covered by snow and ice and beginning Friday night (2/21/20) Chief was removing the impacted snow, and excavating the pad as needed (Photo #2). They are continuing to screen with a soil conductivity meter and are removing any impacted soil. The soil is currently on containment and will be covered until containers are brought to the pad and the material is disposed of in a landfill (Photo #3. 4). Due to the volume of the release, Chief is required to pursue site remediation in accordance with 25 Pa. Code § 78a.66(c). The result of this inspection is Violations noted.

Comments: Chief Oil & Gas reported a release of approximately 2 barrels of produced fluid at the Czop Pad on 2/21/20. The release occurred the same day it was reported. I arrived onsite at 10:05 on 2/24/20. I talked with Kellon Balum and Darrin, both of Chief when I arrived. The release occurred when a piece of the B section of the well broke and allowed produced fluid to begin to spray onto the pad (Photo #1, center). This section of the wellhead is not typically used and doesn't receive much gas flow. It usually is used for monitoring certain pressures in the well. It is believed that sand flowing up from the well eroded and weakened a portion of the pipe and allowed it to rupture. Gas, at approximately 700 to 800 psi pushed produced fluid through the opening, about 2 inches in diameter. This mist was somewhat directional but was blown over a large portion of the pad by wind. The release occurred sometime between a crew leaving the site and the site operator, Darrin, arriving. This limits the duration of the release to no more than about 1 hour. Based on the time and rate of release Chief believes approximately 2 barrels of fluid were released. Typically, offsite monitoring equipment is used to detect events such as this, however, equipment was frozen, and the event was undetected. Much of the pad was covered by snow and ice and beginning Friday night (2/21/20) Chief was removing the impacted snow, and excavating the pad as needed (Photo #2). They are continuing to screen with a soil conductivity meter and are removing any impacted soil. The soil is currently on containment and will be covered until containers are brought to the pad and the material is disposed of in a landfill (Photo #3. 4). Due to the volume of the release, Chief is required to pursue site remediation in accordance with 25 Pa. Code § 78a.66(c). The result of this inspection is Violations noted.

Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/25/2024
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8202507
Permit API: 125-23123
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/25/2024
Comments: Inspection 1 of 2:On 09/25/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the POCKY F24 OG Well in Fallowfield Township, Washington County.The following was observed during inspection:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 1).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo 2)-Some corrosion and appeared leaks were observed on the well head and production tank. Some corrosion was observed on production equipment (Photos 3-5). -I observed brown and shiny colored fluid built up near the well head base and surrounding well head fittings. I received elevated readings of 5.74 mS/cm in the base and 5.39 mS/cm around fittings (Photo 6-10).-It appears the fluid has reached the gravel below. I received elevated conductivity readings of 2.23 mS/cm near the base of the well and 8.67 mS/cm, 8.71 mS/cm and 10.32 mS/cm surrounding the well head.-I observed an open threaded valve that is not plugged and there is appeared elevated fluids leaking from the head. Elevated readings of 9.25 mS/cm (Photo 15 and 16).-3.8 pS/cm on metal on well head components (Photo 17).-I observed tubing coming from production tanks laying on the berm and in yellow container. No elevated readings were found in fluid of the container (Photo 21).-Multiple readings were taken surrounding the berm near the tubing and below. Elevated readings of 5.84, 6.11, 3.67, 8.92, 9.00, and 8.32 mS/cm were found on the inside edges of the earth berm near and below the tubing (Photo 18-24).Diversified submitted an order response on August 31st, 2023 of production tank maintenance or removal. Pocky F24 listed as the following: "Last visit date was 08/10/2023 and Tank(s) on location are secure with no visual evidence of a release. Needs attention: NO." The operator was contacted and notified on 09/25/2024.Violations are being issued for: 78.54, 78.57(a). 91.34 (a), SWMA 301.
